item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is materially closer to the frozen contract. It adds the required replayable multipart convenience API while leaving global request and retry behavior untouched. Both patches incorrectly duplicate FilesService.Add instead of routing Upload through it, but B additionally makes a broad, explicitly prohibited RawClient retry refactor and changes Add/Update behavior.","reasons":["A reuses multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", yielding the required buffered, replayable multipart body.","A preserves FilesService.Add and the shared RawClient/retry machinery, maintaining much better scope discipline.","B changes every io.Reader request by buffering it unless WithNoRetry is set, even when the configured policy may not retry that request. This changes memory use, source-read timing, and error semantics across the SDK.","B explicitly changes Files.Add and Files.Update retry behavior, contrary to the contract's requirement to keep Add behavior unchanged and avoid retry refactoring beyond Upload."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add's option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data error instead of calling s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), violating a central contract requirement and inviting future divergence.","The added tests omit required validation and source-reader-error coverage.","The retry test does not explicitly set RetryAllMethods: true despite exercising a POST, making its intended setup less clear."],"risks_b":["Upload also duplicates Add rather than delegating to it.","The RawClient change is unnecessary and explicitly out of scope; it can buffer arbitrarily large reader bodies throughout the SDK.","It changes the established behavior of the lower-level Add API and unrelated Update requests rather than preserving them as required."]}
